story.title: Apply EU reverse-charge VAT at checkout
story.source_text: As a B2B customer in the EU I don't want to be charged Dutch VAT. Finance keeps refunding these manually.

tracker_meta._note: Copied verbatim from the tracker before refining. Never invented, and never edited to make a rule match.

ask: Who signs this off, and do they need evidence retained beyond the code change?
triage._note: Written by `triage.py apply --write`. The compliance label is why security and data carry real answers rather than 'unchanged', and why the panel includes the stakeholder critic. ABC-131 is a blocks link: the non-EU follow-up cannot start before this ships.

story.summary_human: EU business customers with a valid VAT number registered outside the Netherlands are charged Dutch VAT they do not owe, and Finance refunds it by hand — around 40 orders a month. This story applies the EU reverse-charge rule at checkout: qualifying orders are charged zero VAT with a reason code, and the order summary explains why. Domestic orders and consumer orders keep their current behaviour. Rollout is behind a flag, Netherlands market first.

impacts: Business customers are charged correctly the first time, so they stop asking for a refund
Finance stops reconciling manual corrections for qualifying orders
deliverables: Reverse-charge branch in the rate calculation
A tax object on the order response carrying the reason
A reverse-charge line in the order summary

story.technical_notes_human: `TaxCalculator.rate_for` in api/src/billing/tax.py:88 already resolves rates from the rate table; the reverse-charge branch belongs there. VAT validation landed last sprint in api/src/billing/vat.py:12 and is reused unchanged. The order response is assembled in api/src/api/orders/serializers.py:31 — the new tax object is additive, so web@1.4 keeps working through the deploy window. api/openapi.yaml is edited by S2 only. Money is Decimal throughout (api/src/billing/money.py:17); no floats. Web reads the serialized response and renders in web/src/features/orders/OrderSummary.tsx:64. Flag billing.reverse_charge defaults off; S6 enables it for NL after a week of monitoring zero-VAT order volume.

risks.desc: VIES availability is outside our control and it does go down
risks.mitigation: 3s timeout, fall back to standard rate, log and alert on fallback volume
risks.detection: alert on billing.tax.vies_fallback_rate above 5% over 15 minutes

risks.desc: Charging zero VAT to a customer who does not qualify is a tax exposure
risks.mitigation: flag off by default, NL-only first week, Finance reconciles the first 50 zero-VAT orders
risks.detection: daily zero-VAT order count per market, reviewed by Finance for the first week; a jump outside NL means the flag leaked

risks.desc: A revoked VAT number stays valid for the length of the cache window, so we keep zero-rating a customer who no longer qualifies
risks.mitigation: the TTL is D2's open decision; S0 must price this exposure before a value is chosen
risks.detection: monthly reconciliation against VIES for every VAT number that zero-rated an order

intake.domain_rationale: The EU reverse-charge rule is written down and Finance knows it. Expertise is needed to apply it, but there is a right answer and it is knowable before we build — complicated, not complex. The one genuinely unknowable part, the cache TTL, is D2 and gets a probe.

I don't want to be charged Dutch VAT

dimensions.answer: At checkout, whenever the account carries a validated non-NL EU VAT number.

decisions.question: Where does the reverse-charge rule live?

options.label: In TaxCalculator alongside the rate table
options.tradeoff: one place for all rate logic; TaxCalculator grows

options.label: A separate ReverseChargeRule strategy
options.tradeoff: cleaner boundary; a second place to look for rate behaviour

decisions.chosen: In TaxCalculator alongside the rate table
decisions.rationale: All other rate exceptions already live there; a second location would split the same concern across two files.

decisions.question: Do we cache VIES results, and for how long?

options.label: No cache
options.tradeoff: always current; a VIES outage blocks every B2B checkout

options.label: 24h cache per VAT number
options.tradeoff: survives short outages; a revoked VAT number stays valid for a day

options.label: 30d cache with nightly revalidation
options.tradeoff: cheapest; needs a new scheduled job

decisions.waiting_for: S0's measurement of VIES latency and revocation frequency against a week of real order volume
decisions.expires: before S1 merges — the branch reads the cache, so shipping it forces a default TTL whether or not anyone chose one

open_questions.text: Does Finance need the reverse-charge reason on the invoice PDF this quarter?

Confirm the success signal: manual reverse-charge refunds for qualifying orders reach zero within a month of the NL rollout.

ruled_out.claim: There is no existing VIES client, cache or any VAT-number verification against an external service
ruled_out.conclusion: vat.py:12 validates format only. The lookup is new work; do not go looking for a helper to reuse, and do not mistake VatNumber.is_valid for a verification against VIES.

ruled_out.claim: No shared cache abstraction exists in api - Redis is used directly in two places, with no wrapper
ruled_out.conclusion: Whatever S0 decides, there is no house cache interface to conform to. If a wrapper is wanted, that is a decision, not a detail - raise it rather than inventing one.

ruled_out.claim: The web repo has no tax or VAT logic at all, and no rate table
ruled_out.conclusion: Web only renders what the response carries. Any tax rule implemented there would be a second source of truth - which is why AC4 is a rendering criterion and nothing more.

ruled_out.claim: No existing feature flag covers billing behaviour; billing.reverse_charge is the first
ruled_out.conclusion: There is no established rollout pattern for billing flags to copy. S6 sets the precedent, which is why it carries the removal ticket.

glossary.means: The EU rule that moves VAT liability to the buyer, so the seller charges 0% and the buyer accounts for it. Not a refund, not a discount, and not a zero rate.
The destination country's normal VAT percentage, resolved from the rate table.
The European Commission's VAT number validation service. External, unmetered, and it does go down - see R1.
The code on the tax object explaining which rule applied: reverse-charge | standard-rate | domestic. Customer-visible via the summary, so its values are a contract, not an implementation detail.

critics.attempted: Read the source text against the criteria and the subtask titles. Every outcome in the ask maps to AC1-AC4; the two additions — the reason field and the rollout flag — trace to D1 and D2. Nothing asked for is missing and nothing uninvited was added.

findings.claim: S4's brief edited the German locale file while Q2 — which locales ship on day one — was still open, and nothing in the brief bounded the locale set.
findings.failure: An agent adding the tax line follows the i18n convention, finds every file under src/i18n/locales/, and adds machine-invented German tax wording that no reviewer ever saw, to customers who read it as legal text.
findings.resolution: Added the forbidden entry pinning the set to nl and de until Q2 is answered.

findings.claim: AC2 folds 'unverifiable' in with missing and malformed, so a VIES outage and an invalid VAT number are one case with one expected outcome.
findings.failure: An implementer treats a VIES timeout as an invalid number and charges 19 percent German VAT to a business customer whose number is valid — and every acceptance test still passes.
findings.resolution: Deliberate. Falling back to the standard rate during an outage over-charges, which is refundable; the reverse is not. S0's ADR records the exposure at the chosen TTL and S6's alert surfaces a raised fallback rate within 15 minutes.

findings.claim: TaxCalculator.rate_for was cited at api/src/billing/tax.py:41. Line 41 is the rate table constant; the method is not there.
findings.failure: The agent opens tax.py:41, finds a dict literal, and either edits the rate table directly or spends its context budget hunting for the real method — the exact wandering the brief exists to prevent.
findings.resolution: Re-opened the file: rate_for is at line 88. Corrected in the notes and in evidence.change_surface.

findings.claim: The rollout subtask depended on S1 alone, so the flag could be enabled while the customer-facing summary line was still unshipped.
findings.failure: Enabling billing.reverse_charge for NL without S4 shows business customers a zero-VAT total with no explanation of why — the support load this story exists to remove.
findings.resolution: S6 now depends on S4, which transitively orders it behind S1 and S2.

findings.claim: The criteria described four VAT-number states and two customer types in prose, so nobody could tell whether every combination had an expected outcome.
findings.failure: A consumer with an unverifiable VAT number is a combination no criterion mentions; the implementer picks a behaviour, and whichever they pick, no test disagrees with them.
findings.resolution: Added story.decision_table. All 16 combinations are now covered by a rule, and DT001 fails the bundle if a future edit opens a hole.

findings.claim: 0.25 days for contract tests over a new response field reads as an estimate written to fit the cap.
findings.failure: S3 overruns and takes the wave it shares with S4 and S5 with it, so the rollout slips a day without anyone deciding to slip it.
findings.resolution: The serializer change and its own tests are S2's work; S3 adds cases to the existing tests/contract suite in the style S2 already established. The estimate covers assertions only, which is what the brief's change_surface shows.
